name: Douban Read
tagline: Douban's ebook store and reading app, with original Chinese titles, serialized fiction and per-book or subscription purchases.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You are not paying for the reader, you are paying for the books. Douban Read sells licensed Chinese ebooks plus its own commissioned and serialized originals, which do not exist anywhere else in a form you can legally acquire. An agent can absolutely build you a clean EPUB reader with progress sync, highlights and a library shelf in an afternoon, and it will probably be nicer than the app. It just opens files you already own, which is a different product. The catalog is the whole thing.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted EPUB library and reader that tracks reading position, highlights and notes across your own devices.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to host it
Your own EPUB or PDF files, legally obtained
A browser; no app store needed
whatYouLose: The catalog: licensed Chinese ebooks and Douban's own originals and serials, which you cannot buy elsewhere
Authors publishing chapter by chapter, plus the comment threads under those chapters
Ratings, reviews and lists tied to the wider Douban graph
Polished mobile apps with offline sync and vertical Chinese typography edge cases handled
Purchases and subscription entitlements that follow your account
moatNotes: Licensing plus a native author base plus Douban's review graph. Three moats stacked, and the reader UI is the least important part.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the reader is a commodity and the library is not. Douban Read holds Chinese-language rights and a stable of writers who serialize there specifically because the Douban audience shows up and argues in the comments. A personal reader gets you good typography and your own highlights, which is genuinely worth building, but it cannot conjure the next chapter of a book only published on that platform. Paying is how you get the text at all.
notes: The reader is a weekend build; the bookshelf it needs to fill is not. The moat is Chinese ebook licensing plus authors who serialize only there and readers who follow them.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted personal ebook library and reader as a web app. Single user, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- SvelteKit with TypeScript, Node adapter
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/library.db
- epub.js for rendering EPUB in the browser
- Tailwind for styling
- Run with: npm run dev, and a documented npm run build + node build for the VPS

What it does:
1. Ingest: watch ./data/books for .epub files. On startup and via a Rescan button, parse metadata (title, author, language, cover, description) with a server side EPUB parser, extract the cover image to ./data/covers, and upsert a row keyed by file hash.
2. Shelf: grid of covers with title, author, percent read, last opened. Filters for unread / reading / finished. Search across title and author. Handle CJK titles correctly, do not assume Latin script anywhere.
3. Reader: full screen epub.js reader. Paginated and scrolled modes. Font size, line height, serif/sans toggle, light/sepia/dark themes. Remember all of these per book. Keyboard arrows and click zones for page turns.
4. Position: persist CFI reading position on every relocation, debounced. Reopening a book returns to the exact spot. Since state lives on the server, any device on your LAN resumes correctly, that is the whole sync story.
5. Highlights and notes: select text, save a highlight with optional note. Highlights render on re-open. A per book notes panel listing all highlights with jump-to links, plus export to Markdown.
6. Stats: minutes read per day derived from reader session pings, shown as a simple bar chart for the last 60 days. No external chart library, hand rolled SVG.

Explicitly out of scope: any store or purchase flow, DRM of any kind, PDF rendering, native mobile apps, user accounts, social features, recommendations.

Secrets: none required. If you add an optional metadata lookup, read the key from .env and ship .env.example. Never commit .env.

Deliver a README with setup, where to drop EPUB files, and how to back up ./data. Seed with nothing; the shelf should render an honest empty state telling the user to drop files in ./data/books.
